title: Small Hours: the Threshold
poem: i.  A photograph insists: this happened, this was warm.
ii.  I remember a room I have never stood in. The light there is always late.
iii.  They tell me the rain is only weather. Then why does it knock to be let in.
iv.  What I miss most is a place I am not certain ever stood.
v.  I counted my breaths to be sure they were mine. The number changes.
colophon: rings around a center that drifted while you watched.
